title: an unrecognized manifest-level `pattern` value is rejected by name (manifest-level counterpart to row 2)
error_substring: is not a supported plugin family (expected one of
why: This checks the same unrecognized-pattern rule as row02, but at the
manifest level across all manifest-loading doors, instead of at the
sidecar level. The two fixtures pin the same underlying rule at each of
the two levels; it is normal for both to be numbered as the same row.
Both C++ registries and Python's manifest loader already rejected an
unrecognized manifest pattern; this fixture is the first place that
cross-language behaviour is checked mechanically rather than just observed.
The C++ and Python rejection messages differ in wording (C++ appends an
upgrade hint and lists the supported patterns differently from Python), so
this fixture only checks the literal text the two messages share.
